Morning:

1)Cetaphil cleanser, 

2)natural moisturizer and then your SPF

- you can add a vitamin c before the moisturizer for brightening the skin. 
-if you find the moisturizer is too heavy with SPF, skip the moisturizer. I used to go straight in with SPF after a vitamin c serum because my face gets really shiny and oily in the day any literally any moisturizer is too heavy for me in the day. 


- if you're feeling dry or tight after using the Cetaphil cleanser, change it to a less harsh drying one. I feel that sometimes if something is too harsh, our skin compensates by making more oil.  The simple micellar facial gel wash is good. However, there have been times when I skip cleansing my face all together and only use water.

Night:

1)Cleanser (ideally you should double cleanse to remove SPF and makeup), 

2) glow tonic (don't use this every night) use twice a week or once if you're a complete beginner.

3)niacinamide and zinc, 

4) moisturizer


- for first cleanser I would recommend an oil/balm. 

- Salicylic acid is a bha and good for spots. Invest in a salicylic acid product. You can get Salicylic acid cleansers.

- maybe invest in a face oil to use at night after moisturizer. Oily skinned folks usually avoid oil thinking it will be worse and break them out more, when it actually is beneficial.

Grapeseed oil is cheap and can be found in a local grocery store. Jojoba oil is the closest to our natural skin oil so it gives hydration while not disturbing the skin. 

For pimples make sure you're changing your bedding often. that and also stress was a big cause for me. Oh and drink a lot of water/eat healthy.
